title: Dada, Zurich, Paris and Berlin, 1917–1921 — the journal Dada (nos. 1–8), Der Dada no. 1, Tzara, Picabia, Serner and Ball
edition: Dada: recueil littéraire et artistique, nos. 1–8, ed. Tristan Tzara (Zürich, July 1917 – Paris, September 1921) — scans of all eight issues, with their text layers; Tristan Tzara, Vingt-cinq poèmes, with ten woodcuts by Hans Arp (Zürich: Collection Dada, 1918); Francis Picabia, Poèmes et dessins de la fille née sans mère: 18 dessins, 51 poèmes (Lausanne: Imprimeries réunies, 1919; 'Terminé à Gstaad, 5 avril 1918'); Francis Picabia, Pensées sans langage, poème, preceded by a preface by 'Udnie' (Paris: Eugène Figuière, 1919), dedicated to Ribemont-Dessaignes, Duchamp and Tzara; Der Dada, no. 1, ed. Raoul Hausmann (Berlin, June 1919) — scan; Walter Serner, Letzte Lockerung: manifest dada (Hannover: Paul Steegemann, 1920) — Google Books copy; Hugo Ball, Flametti, oder vom Dandysmus der Armen, Roman (1918), dedicated to Emmy Hennings; Adolf Knoblauch, Dada, with a woodcut by Lyonel Feininger (Leipzig: Kurt Wolff, Der jüngste Tag, 1919)

license.payload: Public domain in the United States: every item published 1917–1921. EU status per author: PD-EU — Ball (d. 1927), Serner (d. 1942), Picabia (d. 1953), Knoblauch (d. 1951); NOT PD-EU — Tzara (d. 1963), Arp (d. 1966), Hausmann (d. 1971), Feininger (d. 1956 → 2027). Payload/record split per EA-CORPORA-02/01. Project Gutenberg packaging under the PG licence.

normalization: Project Gutenberg texts stripped at the START/END markers, CRLF to LF, otherwise unaltered; Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt) — the scan under original/<identifier>/ is the witness; Wikisource texts as rendered from the proofread transcription, page headings marked '=== title ==='.
scope: Cabaret Voltaire (Zürich, 1916) is on the Internet Archive only in the 1981 reprint and is not seated. Ball's sound poems ('Karawane', 'Gadji beri bimba') were printed in the Dada Almanach (Berlin, 1920), not located in a public-domain witness; QUEUED. Schwitters's Anna Blume (1919) not located; Ursonate (1932) is in copyright in the United States until 2028.
verified_loci: Dada 3 (December 1918) — Tzara's manifesto of 1918, opening 'Pour lancer un manifeste' (the text layer reads 'il faut vouioir' for 'il faut vouloir')
Vingt-cinq poèmes (1918) — the Arp woodcuts credited
Serner, Letzte Lockerung (1920) — the title, in the text layer
Picabia, Pensées sans langage (1919) — the dedication to Ribemont-Dessaignes, Marcel Duchamp and Tristan Tzara
why_seated: The negation the archive's negative ontology has to stand next to. Dada declares that the work is its own refusal, and the journal is where the refusal was printed as a programme, issue by issue.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-15: "we need more seatings of avant garde literature. dada. farce. oulipo. futurist. - whatevers in the public domain. originals is good on classics, impoverished on modern. and i want the italian troubadours. and pound, more pound. need the cantos." — "and the concrete poets" — "also need jarry, shklovsky, etc" — "it gets an ea-corpora deposit and a spine and a card on tll, bulk seatings per ea-corpora deposit is fine".
